beats.text: He ruled four continents. From a desk.
Philip the Second was twenty-eight when his exhausted father handed him Spain, the Netherlands, Italy, and the Americas.
Even the Philippines are named after him.
He married four times. One wife was Queen Mary of England, so for four years, he was king of England too.
He built El Escorial, a palace and monastery in one. From a small office inside, he read every report himself.
Spaniards called him the Paper King.
His son, Don Carlos, grew unstable. Philip had him locked up. Six months later, Carlos was dead.
Enemies said the king had killed his own son. No one has ever proved it.
At Lepanto, his fleet crushed the Ottoman navy. A wounded soldier on board was named Miguel de Cervantes.
Then he took the crown of Portugal. Now the sun truly never set on his empire.
But it all ran on borrowed silver. And one queen was about to challenge him.
